Position: Full Time, Permanent

Our client, Khosa Concrete & Landscaping Pty Ltd, located in Huntingdale, Western Australia, is a growing construction business specialising in high-quality concreting, landscaping and outdoor construction solutions throughout the Perth metropolitan area. The company delivers a broad range of residential and commercial projects, including concrete driveways, pathways, patios, retaining walls, paving, fencing, timber structures, artificial turf installations and complete landscape transformations. 

Due to continued business growth and an increasing volume of construction projects, our client is seeking an experienced and motivated Carpenter to join its skilled construction team. The successful applicant will undertake a variety of carpentry works associated with building interiors, outdoor living spaces and structural construction, while ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently and to the highest quality standards.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications to determine materials, dimensions and installation requirements. 
-	Measure, cut, shape, assemble and install timber, plywood and other building materials to required specifications. 
-	Construct, install and repair timber frameworks, wall frames, floor systems, roof structures, partitions and ceilings. 
-	Install doors, windows, skirting boards, architraves, staircases, cabinetry and other interior and exterior timber fittings. 
-	Build and install pergolas, decking, fencing, gates and other outdoor timber structures. 
-	Carry out first-fix and second-fix carpentry works for residential and commercial building projects. 
-	Undertake formwork construction where required to support building and landscaping projects. 
-	Repair and maintain existing timber structures, fixtures and fittings to ensure structural integrity and appearance. 
-	Operate, maintain and inspect carpentry tools, machinery and equipment in a safe and efficient manner. 
-	Estimate material requirements and assist in ordering timber and construction materials. 
-	Ensure all carpentry works comply with Australian building codes, project specifications and workplace health and safety requirements. 
-	Liaise professionally with clients, supervisors and other trades to ensure projects are completed on time and to a high standard.

Skills & Qualifications

-	AQF Certificate III in Carpentry (or equivalent trade qualification), including at least two years of structured on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV in a relevant trade.
-	Minimum one year of relevant full-time experience as a Carpenter.
-	Ability to accurately read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications.
-	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building materials and safe work practices.
-	High attention to detail with excellent workmanship and problem-solving abilities.
-	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
-	Good organisational and time management skills with the ability to meet project deadlines.
-	Sound understanding of Australian Workplace Health and Safety requirements.

Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.
To apply for this position, email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Murdoch

Join a leading private hospital as a Security Officer and play a vital role in ensuring a safe and secure environment for patients, visitors, and staff. This position is responsible for delivering a comprehensive security service across the Murdoch hospital campus, maintaining safety, managing access control, and supporting emergency response activities.

You will conduct regular patrols, monitor hospital facilities and car parks, respond to incidents, and provide timely reporting and risk mitigation recommendations. The role also involves operating security systems including CCTV and access control, coordinating with emergency services where required, and maintaining strict confidentiality at all times.

This is an excellent opportunity for a proactive and professional security officer who is committed to safety, customer service, and contributing to a supportive healthcare environment.

The Position

Undertake regular patrols and active surveillance of Murdoch Hospital buildings and grounds including Hospice, Wexford and Murdoch Medical Clinics, SurgiCentre, Belmont House and car parks.

Investigate all incidents relating to breaches of physical and personal security and loss of property and prepares written reports on same.

Provide reports and recommendations directed to the prevention of incidents and adverse occurrences, and provides security risk management services to patients, staff and property.

Provide appropriate and immediate response to any call for assistance and liaises with law enforcement and other external agencies.

Operate the Hospital security systems, including access control software, issuing of security cards and CCTV systems.

Maintain complete confidentiality on sensitive security and medical matters.

Conduct internal cash and drug escorts as required.

Receive, record, store and dispatch found and patient property.

Operate the Hospital fire systems and respond to emergency situations according to the Emergency Procedures Manual.

Assist in conducting fire and evacuation drills throughout the Hospital.

Assist as part of the Medical Emergency Response Team afterhours under direction of the Duty Manager.

Maintain traffic and parking controls in accordance with Murdoch Hospital policies and procedures.

Perform minor repairs and maintenance to parking equipment.

Assist Engineering after hours by patrolling plant rooms, monitoring equipment, fixing minor issues and reporting irreparable problems to the Duty Manager.

Assist Nursing Caregiver's with morgue duties.

Undertake other duties as directed by Manager Security & Parking.

Undertake other duties as directed afterhours by the Duty Manager, such as moving beds, collection of blood from blood bank, and escorting visitors and patients through the hospital.

You will have experience in control rooms and access control software with knowledge of workplace safety including WH&S, fire panels, detection equipment, electronic access systems and CCTV systems.

Holding effective communication, conflict resolution, negotiation and problem solving skills you will have the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment. Intermediate computer skills and well-developed verbal and written communication skills including completion of reports will be required.

To succeed you will hold a Security Monitoring Officer Licence and Security Officer Licence.

Above all, people will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer you

Casual Rate: $48.70 to $50.91 per hour, (inclusive of casual loading) plus 12% superannuation

Casual positions available

As a casual employee, you can salary package a percentage of your earnings each pay period on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses 

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Employee support through our dedicated free Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Innovative Professional Development opportunities

All applicants are asked to submit a covering letter (of no more than two (2) pages) demonstrating how you meet the above position requirements. 

For enquiries contact Ashlee Lewis, Manager Security and Parking, on (08) 9428 8511.

Applications will be reviewed throughout the advertising period and interviews conducted regularly. Apply today!

Our commitment is to create a safe and nurturing environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care and proactively take steps to protect them from abuse, ensuring their safety and well-being. 

Our inclusive culture fosters an environment that is respectful and secure, welcoming and accessible, and unified through our diverse community.    Click here to Apply now →

Pressure Welder

•	Permanent Role 
•	$85k-$90k PA 
•	Pinkenba QLD

POSITION

Full-time position for a Pressure Welder is available in Pinkenba, QLD, 4008.

SKILLS

At least an AQF Certificate III, including at least two years of on-the-job training or a Certificate Ivin a relevant field. At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualification. In addition to the qualification at least one year of relevant work experience is required.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Pressure Welder is responsible for assembling, welding, inspecting, testing and repairing pressure vessels, pipes, pipelines, boilers, tanks and associated pressure-containing components in accordance with engineering drawings, approved welding procedures, relevant Australian Standards and industry specifications.
The role requires precision welding using MMAW, GTAW (TIG), GMAW (MIG) and FCAW processes on carbon steel, stainless steel and alloy materials in workshop and site environments.

POSITION DUTIES

•	Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, welding procedure specifications and technical specifications to determine job requirements and appropriate welding techniques for pressure systems.
•	Select, measure, cut, shape, bend, bevel, clean and prepare metal sections and pipes using hand tools, heating equipment and metalworking machinery.
•	Align, fit and secure pipes, vessel components and other pressure-containing components before welding.
•	Assemble, weld and repair pressure vessels, pipes, pipelines, boilers and tanks to relevant standards and approved welding procedures.
•	Operate welding equipment using MMAW, GTAW (TIG), GMAW (MIG) and FCAW
processes.
•	Weld in various positions, including vertical and overhead positions, and in confined spaces where required.
•	Conduct pre-heating, post-weld heat treatment, stress-relief and finishing processes as specified.
•	Examine welds for bead width, penetration, precision, defects and compliance with applicable standards and specifications.
•	Conduct or assist with pressure, leak and other weld-integrity testing to confirm that pressure-containing systems meet required standards.
•	Repair defective welds and complete rework in accordance with approved procedures.
•	Clean and smooth welds by grinding, filing, chiselling and polishing as required.
•	Perform routine inspection and maintenance of welding equipment and report equipment defects. 
•	Comply with workplace health and safety requirements, permit systems and safe work procedures.
•	Work collaboratively with fabricators, boilermakers, inspectors and engineers to complete work to specification.

ADDITIONAL ATTRIBUTES

•	Willingness to learn and develop new skills
•	Strong communication skills
•	High level of attention to detail
•	Commitment to workplace health and safety
•	Effective problem-solving skills
•	Ability to work both independently and as part of a team

SALARY

$85,000 - $90,000 per annum based on experience.

TO APPLY
Applications in Word format should be submitted via our website: 
https://precruitment.com.au/job-seekers/
